records.text: Gul’dan seeks power for his armies through a dark master whose strength he demands others acknowledge. He boasts that this gift will let him raze and reform the land, and claims personal glory for securing his forces’ future. His manner is commanding and grandiose: he orders witnesses to be silent and then to behold the power he is channeling.
A felmist is a gas cloud found in Shadowmoon Valley.

Doomwalker confronts intruders in a terse, machine-like voice, warning that they will be eliminated. During the fight it reports seismic disruption, releases an attack at a set magnitude, locks onto its trajectory, and accelerates; after a kill it reports the threat at zero.

Xi'ri is a naaru directing Sha'tar forces in the campaign against Illidan at the Black Temple. His force is meant to create a distraction so Akama and Maiev can enter, and he supports the effort to find Akama's Deathsworn inside. He is focused on the nearby battle, with his forces awaiting his decision to begin the attack.
Collidus the Warp-Watcher is a powerful demon of Shadowmoon Valley, where he is encountered as a hostile opponent.

Ambassador Jerrikar bears the title Servant of Illidan and is a high-ranking demon found across several areas of Shadowmoon Valley. In combat he uses Dark Strike and a power named Diplomatic Immunity.
Kraator is a powerful demon encountered in Shadowmoon Valley. He fights with Conflagration and Inferno.
Brubeck Stormfoot is a Gryphon Master who handles flight service. His flight dialogue asks travelers where they would like to go; when attacked, he calls for guards and can summon an enraged gryphon.
Drek'Gol is a Wind Rider Master who handles flight service. When attacked, he calls for guards and can summon an enraged wyvern.
Darg Bloodclaw is an innkeeper who speaks of rest for battle-weary visitors, making these new lands their own, and sharing stories by the fire.

Grokom Deatheye is an orc weaponsmith eager to turn the Legion's demon-destroying weapons against their makers. He recognizes the rare metal and runes as an opportunity to forge a useful weapon. When the work exceeds his ability, he reluctantly recommends the human smith David Wayne, acknowledging expertise beyond his own despite Wayne's former Alliance ties.

Korthul is Shadowmoon Village’s bowyer and gunsmith, offering weapons-related goods and repairs. His trade centers on bows and firearms, giving him a distinct place among the village’s smithing and general-supply services.
Grutah is a master blacksmithing trainer. Grutah offers instruction to smiths who have honed their skills enough, and speaks of the craft as knowledge personally taught.
Krek Cragcrush supplies blacksmithing goods and also offers browsing and repair services, distinguishing his trade from general and trade-goods stalls.

Trop Rendlimb is a general-goods vendor in Shadowmoon Village, offering customers goods to browse. His listed trade is broad general supply rather than the village’s specialized blacksmithing, weapon, or trade-goods services.

Kalara deals in trade goods in Shadowmoon Village, offering goods for customers to browse. Her listed specialty is trade goods, distinct from the village’s general-goods and blacksmithing-supply services.
Targrom is a food and drink vendor in the Wildhammer settlement, offering goods to visitors.
Daggle Ironshaper supplies guns and ammunition and offers repairs in the Wildhammer settlement.
Dreg Cloudsweeper is an innkeeper. His greeting asks visitors where they would like to fly.
A Wildhammer Guard, one of the rank-bearing guards posted around the area.
A Shadowmoon Peon, a worker stationed in the area.

A Kor'kron Defender who keeps the peons in line with grim, sardonic threats: he warns that lazy workers may be launched by catapult toward the Black Temple and jokes that the nearby graveyard is where they can take a break.
A Kor'kron rider in Shadowmoon Valley.
Crinn Pathfinder serves as a stable master at Wildhammer Stronghold. He helps visitors stable pets and recover lost companions.
Celie Steelwing is a cook.

Ordinn Thunderfist is a hammersmith at Wildhammer Stronghold who works to turn captured Legion anti-demon weapons into arms against the Legion. He recognizes the shard's demon-slaying enchantment and, finding one smithing attempt beyond his ability, directs the ingots to the more capable David Wayne.
Dalin Stouthammer is a cooking-supplies vendor in Shadowmoon Valley; visitors can browse his goods.
Oran Blusterbrew is a Trade Goods vendor at the local settlement. Visitors can browse his wares; his role is a general merchandise shop rather than a specialist craft.
Mari Stonehand is an armorsmith who sells goods and repairs equipment. Her work gives travelers a place to maintain their armor and browse for supplies at the local settlement.
Salle Sunforge is a General Goods vendor whose wares include ammunition. Travelers can browse for everyday supplies and ammunition at the local settlement.

Eli Thunderstrike cares for Sky'ree, commander Kurdran's gryphon, when Kurdran is busy. Eli admires her beauty, strength and fierceness, praises her loyalty to Kurdran, and considers caring for her an honor.
Sky'ree is Kurdran Wildhammer's gryphon. Her keeper, Eli Thunderstrike, praises her beauty, strength and fierceness, and believes she would die for Kurdran. Eli considers caring for her an honor.
Wildhammer Gryphon Riders are mounted personnel associated with the Wildhammer, identified by their gryphon-riding role.
A Wildhammer scout operating in Outland.

Barimoke Wildbeard challenges Bron to hit him, first with fists and then with a hammer. He urges Bron on with an insult when he hesitates, then enthusiastically approves the blow. Barimoke is eager for a rough contest with Bron.

Bron Goldhammer is cautious about Barimoke's demand: he questions whether it should be with fists and warns that Barimoke may get hurt. His perplexed reaction and hesitant replies contrast with Barimoke's insistence on being hit.
A Scryer Guardian serving as a protector in Outland.
Alorra is an armorer who offers goods and repairs. The available records identify her work but provide no personal history or views.
Feranin is a food and drink merchant. The available records identify his trade but provide no personal history or views.
Lelagar supplies blacksmithing materials and offers repairs. The available records identify his trade but provide no personal history or views.
Arrond sells tailoring supplies. The available records identify his trade but provide no personal history or views.
Dunaman is a weapons vendor who also offers repairs. The available records identify his trade but provide no personal history or views.
Nanomah is a provisions merchant who sells food and drink. The available records identify her trade but provide no personal history or views.
Darmend is a blacksmithing-supplies merchant.
Dearny is a leatherworking merchant.
Maddix is a flight master. In combat, he summons an enraged gryphon and wyvern.
Alorya is a general-goods merchant.
Belanna is a humanoid in Shadowmoon Valley.
Sulamin is a humanoid in Shadowmoon Valley.
Furan is a humanoid in Shadowmoon Valley.
Denath is a humanoid in Shadowmoon Valley.
Harram is a humanoid in Shadowmoon Valley.
Maranem is a humanoid in Shadowmoon Valley.
Dorni is a General Goods vendor in Outland. The shop interaction offers a chance to browse goods.
A demon known as Wrathwalker.
A Dreadwarden serving Illidan in Shadowmoon Valley.
A Deathforge tinkerer.
A Mo'arg weaponsmith.
A Deathforge smith tied to the forge's infernal-summoning work: adventurers seek an Elemental Displacer from a smith or tinkerer to disrupt the summoning ritual.
An infernal identified as newly crafted among the Deathforge's constructs.
A cooling infernal among the Deathforge's constructs.
A Coilskar Defender is a humanoid found in Shadowmoon Valley.
A Coilskar Myrmidon serves the Coilskar force with disciplined resolve, answering “Understood” and insisting, “We will not fail.”
A Coilskar Sorceress keeps watch for intruders and urges vigilance. Her warning that they must not fail “the master” shows loyalty to a superior, while her water magic serves in combat.
A humanoid bearing the designation Coilskar Siren.
A Coilskar Screamer is a humanoid found in Shadowmoon Valley.
Coilskar Cobras are serpents found among the Coilskar population; they attack with a venomous strike.
A Coilskar Muckwatcher in Zangarmarsh, the Muckwatcher is identified by its watch role. It casts spells during combat and when it draws an attacker’s attention.
A Coilskar Waterkeeper, identified by the waterkeeping role in its name.
An Eclipsion Centurion stationed in Shadowmoon Valley. It is a rank-bearing combatant; its recorded combat ability is Spellbreaker.
An Eclipsion Blood Knight stationed in Shadowmoon Valley, identified by its knightly title and blood-knight role.
An Eclipsion Archmage in Shadowmoon Valley. It is a spellcaster whose recorded combat ability is Ancient Fire.
An Illidari Dreadbringer, explicitly titled a servant of Illidan, in Zangarmarsh. It uses recorded spells in combat and when it draws an attacker’s attention.
An Illidari Painlasher, titled Servant of Illidan, is one of several stationed in Outland’s Shadowmoon Valley. It casts a spell while fighting.
An Illidari Agonizer is one of several found in Outland’s Shadowmoon Valley. It casts a spell while fighting.
An Illidari Shocktrooper, titled Servant of Illidan, is among the Illidari encountered in Shadowmoon Valley. It casts combat spells, including one cast when attacked.
An Eclipsion Bloodwarder encountered in Shadowmoon Valley, it is associated with the Eclipsion forces. Its behavior includes summoning an Eclipsion Hawkstrider when it dies.
A Crazed Colossus found in Shadowmoon Valley.
A Son of Corok encountered in Shadowmoon Valley, it belongs to a group named among the foes to clear from the path in “Breaching the Path.” Its behavior includes a combat spell.
An undead talonite of the Dark Conclave whose abilities include Shroud of Death and Talon of Justice.
An undead shadowmancer of the Dark Conclave whose abilities include Fear and Shroud of Death.
An undead ravenguard of the Dark Conclave whose abilities include Shroud of Death and Piercing Howl, and who can become enraged.
A mechanical naga distiller at Coilskar Point.
A blue wind rider in the Eclipse Point area of Outland.
A tawny wind rider in the Eclipse Point area of Outland.
A swift green wind rider in the Eclipse Point area of Outland.
A swift purple wind rider in the Eclipse Point area of Outland.
A swift red wind rider in the Eclipse Point area of Outland.
A swift yellow wind rider in the Eclipse Point area of Outland.
A green wind rider in the Eclipse Point area of Outland.

Dama Wildmane is the wind rider keeper at Shadowmoon Village, where she oversees the care and training of wyverns. She describes them as hardy mounts trained for Draenor’s severe weather, while also facing pressure to meet demand from buyers and outposts.

Olrokk is Shadowmoon Village’s riding trainer, teaching visitors to ride their own flying mounts. He stresses that flight takes training, dedication, and gold, and directs learners to Dama Wildmane to buy a wind rider. In an exchange, he reacts to Nutral’s draenei referral with contempt.
Eclipsion Dragonhawks are dragonhawk creatures found across Shadowmoon Valley. They use Fire Breath in combat.
An Ebon Gryphon is a gryphon creature found in Shadowmoon Valley.
A Golden Gryphon is a gryphon creature found in Shadowmoon Valley.
The Snowy Gryphon Mount is a gryphon creature found in Shadowmoon Valley.
A swift green riding gryphon found in the Wildhammer Stronghold area of Shadowmoon Valley.
A swift purple riding gryphon found in the Wildhammer Stronghold area of Shadowmoon Valley.
A swift red riding gryphon found in the Wildhammer Stronghold area of Shadowmoon Valley.
A swift blue riding gryphon found in the Wildhammer Stronghold area of Shadowmoon Valley.

Brunn Flamebeard is a Wildhammer gryphon keeper, proud of the stock in his care. He welcomes visitors to consider his gryphons and reacts furiously to Nutral’s proposal to bolt gadgets and a rocket onto them, insisting he will tolerate no additions beyond a saddle.

Ilsa Blusterbrew is a Wildhammer riding trainer who speaks warmly and with a teasing humor about learning to fly. She charges for instruction, thanks Nutral for sending her business, and points visitors to Brunn for gryphons.

Grand Commander Ruusk expects deference and resents interruption. At Eclipse Point, Borak plans to fool him with a disguised messenger posing as a superior, claiming orders from Ruusk’s lord Illidan about moving the cipher.
Prophetess Cavrylin is a demon who uses Melt Flesh and Chaos Nova in combat.
Lady Shav'rar is a humanoid in Shadowmoon Valley.
The Keeper of the Cistern uses Water Bolt in combat and Frost Nova against nearby opponents.
A Deathforge summoner among the Shadow Council forces guarding the entrance to the Deathforge, where Ewan Wildwing seeks a way inside.
A Deathforge guardian among the Shadow Council forces guarding the entrance to the Deathforge. Uses Piercing Strike in combat.
A Deathforge demon, this imp is a combatant that holds its ground once battle begins.

An Earthen Ring earthmender, Torlok seeks to make amends with spirits harmed by his people and asks for their wisdom, warning allies that the spirits may lash out. He presses a spirit for knowledge of Cyrukh and vows his allies will destroy the fire lord; a spirit’s cryptic warning leaves him wondering what its sign means.
Earthmender Gorboto belongs to the Earthen Ring and serves as a quest contact.

Earthmender Wilda of the Earthen Ring investigated distressed water spirits and discovered naga fouling Shadowmoon Valley’s water supply before being taken prisoner. Wilda seeks escape and protection to break the captives’ bonds, senses tortured spirits nearby, and invokes the Earthmother’s care for a rescuer.
A captive water elemental who expresses gratitude to an earthmender.
Spirits of the past address Gul’dan with conflicting cries: pleas to spare their young and warnings that the elements will not forgive them, alongside calls to tear the land apart and sever the tie.
An enraged earth elemental.

An enraged water spirit roaming Shadowmoon Valley. Earthmender Torlok says these spirits are found around the region's agitated water, where they howl to the land in anguish; he asks adventurers to capture their souls with his totem.

An enraged air spirit that roams Shadowmoon Valley's Netherwing Fields, among the great blue crystals and the surrounding cliffs and mountain bases. Earthmender Torlok describes these spirits as tortured and asks adventurers to capture their souls with his totem.
An enraged fire spirit in Shadowmoon Valley. Earthmender Torlok says the region's enraged fire spirits are among those whose souls he seeks to commune with and capture using his totem.
A dormant infernal in Shadowmoon Valley. Its reset behavior casts Stationary Infernal Ball once, keeping it in a stationary, dormant state.

Uvuros is a powerful fel beast hunted in Shadowmoon Valley. Wanted notices describe it as a threat and call for its death, with its fiery mane sought as proof. The notices place it near the Hand of Gul’dan, though their directions differ on which stronghold lies northeast.
The Spawn of Uvuros is a creature identified by its relationship to Uvuros. Its name and animal form mark it as part of the same bestial line.
A Kor’kron wyvern rider: a mounted member of the named Kor’kron force encountered in Hellfire Peninsula.

Netharel is an Illidari demon hunter and one of three night elf masters assisting Varedis at the Ruins of Karabor training grounds. The Aldor and Scryers both name Netharel among those they seek to defeat as part of shutting down the academy.
An Illidari dreadlord encountered in Shadowmoon Valley.

Theras is a night elf Illidari demon hunter and one of the three masters who assist Varedis at the Ruins of Karabor training grounds. The Aldor and Scryers each seek to close the academy of Illidan imitators, naming Theras among those who must be stopped.

Alandien is a night elf Illidari demon hunter and one of the three masters who assist Varedis at the Ruins of Karabor training grounds. Both the Aldor and Scryers name him among those they seek to stop as they try to shut down the academy of Illidan imitators.

Varedis is an Illidari demon hunter at the center of the training grounds in the Ruins of Karabor, assisted by three night elf masters. The Aldor and Scryers seek to shut down his academy of Illidan imitators. Their plans call for using the Book of Fel Names when he enters Metamorphosis, to weaken him.
Demon Hunter Supplicants are numerous humanoid combatants at the Ruins of Karabor. They cast a spell when they gain an opponent's attention and use another as a fight wears on and their health drops.
Demon Hunter Initiates are trainees at the Ruins of Karabor, among the academy of Illidan imitators that Varedis oversees. Many are present at the grounds, and they cast a spell in combat.

Oronok Torn-heart poses as a farmer while using trained felboars to dig tubers from the Shattered Plains, but admits the farming role was a test. He offers shelter by his fire, trades, and tells the story of the Cipher of Damnation; the flayers' attacks on his boars have made their nest a personal concern. He also sends the listener to find his sons.
A domesticated felboar found around Shadowmoon Valley, including the Shattered Plains and Oronok's Farm.
A ravenous flayer found on the Shattered Plains in Shadowmoon Valley. It can cast an ability when wounded in combat.
The Ravenous Flayer Matriarch is a solitary den mother among the flayers of the Shattered Plains; in combat, she casts the Den Mother's Mark.
Summoner Skartax is in Shadowmoon Valley. On appearing, he casts a personal aura and begins a channel.
An invisible Deathforge caster.
Umberhowl is Oronok's companion, a beast found in Shadowmoon Valley's Deathforge region.
Warbringer Razuun is a Legion overseer associated with operations at the Deathforge. The Alliance and Horde both seek to bring him down and recover his orders.

Grom'tor is Oronok Torn-heart's firstborn son and the family's warrior. His father describes him as ill-tempered and bloodthirsty. Seeking a fragment of the Cipher of Damnation from the Coilskar naga, he uses violence and mocking offers of freedom to interrogate them. He calls the ordeal his “fun.”

Ar'tor is Oronok Torn-heart's youngest son, a skilled hunter and expert tracker whose search of Illidari Point ended in death. Oronok praised his abilities but feared the danger of the demons there. Ar'tor's lifeless body is held by demonic crystal magic; this is his corpse, not a speaking account of his wishes.

Borak, son of Oronok, is an observer and planner focused on the Illidari blood elves and the moving Cipher of Damnation. He has tracked their envoy for weeks and devises an ambush using bloodthistle, then plans an armor disguise to deliver a message to the Grand Commander. His warning urges caution around the bridge.
A Coilskar naga commander encountered in Shadowmoon Valley. The commander asks what is meant, denies that the naga have the cipher, then pleads to be set free.
A Shadow Council warlock among the hostile forces in Shadowmoon Valley. This group appears in numbers and casts a green beam.
A hostile mutant creature encountered in Shadowmoon Valley. It uses Enrage in combat.
Eva is a beast serving as Ar’tor’s guardian.

Painmistress Gabrissa is a demon leader sought at Illidari Point for the Crystalline Key to Ar’tor’s crystal prison. The search treats her as a possible holder of the key. She uses Curse of Pain and Subservience in combat.
A Terrormaster demon who uses Fear and Cleave in combat.
Ruul the Darkener is a formidable figure in Shadowmoon Valley, whose threats promise darkened skies and death. He also takes flight, reinforcing the ominous presence conveyed by his name and words.

Spirit of Ar'tor is the restless spirit of a Torn-heart warrior, still bound near Illidari Point by his unfinished duty to recover a Cipher of Damnation fragment. He asks for his heirloom bow, Lohn'goron, then entrusts the bow and fragment to his father, Oronok. Though he mourns his death, he hopes to reach the glorious hunting grounds once his task is done.

Kurdran Wildhammer helps lead the defense of Wildhammer Stronghold, where his men fight under Wing Commander Nuainn. The Legion’s siege and Illidan’s forces are concerns for the stronghold. Kurdran values valor from allies and expresses gratitude on the Wildhammer clan’s behalf.
Gedrah is a stable master in Hellfire Peninsula. He greets visitors and offers help with stabling pets or recovering lost companions.
An Illidari Shadowstalker is identified as a servant of Illidan and is found among several such figures in Hellfire Peninsula.
Detrafila is Gedrah’s pet, an individual creature identified by name.

Wing Commander Nuainn commands Wildhammer defense at the stronghold against the Burning Legion’s repeated infernal attacks. He describes his troops as ragged and exhausted and says he cannot spare forces for an assault on Legion Hold, so he sends the player to gather intelligence and disrupt the threat. He is resolute about defending the Wildhammer home, while recognizing that Legion and Illidan’s forces both threaten it.

Blood Guard Gulmok is a Horde guard and quest contact at Shadowmoon Village, where he directs the defense against the Legion's attacks. He urgently calls on able-bodied recruits to fight the infernals threatening the village, and sends a disguised operative to learn Legion Hold's plans. He is alarmed by the threat of renewed bombardment and presses for action to protect the settlement.
A humanoid of the Dark Conclave, the Harbinger is associated with the group’s presence in Shadowmoon Valley. It casts Shroud of Death when it respawns.
A humanoid of the Dark Conclave found in Shadowmoon Valley, Scorncrow stands still while out of combat.
A humanoid of the Dark Conclave found around Shadowmoon Valley, Hawkeye uses Enraging Strike in combat.

Anchorite Ceyla praises the naaru and expects the Light to triumph. Ceyla urgently seeks the Baa’ri tablets and Medallion of Karabor to aid the struggle against Illidan, using Akama’s orders to trace the scattered fragments. Ceyla sees an opportunity to turn a Dragonmaw attack against its perpetrators.
A mechanical fel reaver associated with Legion Hold.

Lakaan is an Ashtongue Corruptor of Water, one of four Broken said to have once been powerful shamans and now to defile the elements they revered. A medallion fragment is associated with him; reports place him near Coilskar Point.
An invisible infernal caster.
A corrupt water totem, an elemental object encountered in the Shadowmoon Valley region.
A Skethyl owl, a wild creature found in the region. It can cast a spell when injured.
An Ashtongue Shaman serving Illidan, stationed with the tribe at the Ruins of Baa’ri. The Ashtongue are described as fierce and ruthless Broken handpicked by Akama for Illidan’s forces.
An Ashtongue Warrior serving Illidan, stationed with the tribe at the Ruins of Baa’ri. The Ashtongue are described as fierce and ruthless Broken handpicked by Akama for Illidan’s forces.
An Ashtongue worker in service to Illidan, stationed in Shadowmoon Valley. In combat, it casts a defensive spell.
A greater felfire diemetradon found across Shadowmoon Valley. It ranges through several parts of the region and attacks with Fel Fireball.

Stormer Ewan Wildwing is a scout assigned by Wing Commander Nuainn to observe the Deathforge. Eager to put his hammer to use, he chafes at a mission of watching rather than fighting. He fears for fellow scout Flanis Swiftwing and hopes Flanis's information can help shut down infernal production. He seeks to disrupt the Shadow Council's summoning of the creatures' elemental souls.
Gryphonrider Nordin is a named gryphon rider stationed in Shadowmoon Valley. He is available as a quest giver.

Scout Zagran is an orc scout involved in the effort against the Shadow Council’s Deathforge. He studies reports of infernal launches and directs an assault on the forge’s guards. He calls missing scout Kagrosh a fool for acting recklessly and doubts he survived. Zagran says orders keep him from engaging the enemy himself.
Mokthar Grimblade is a humanoid in Shadowmoon Valley.
A Rocknail flayer in Shadowmoon Valley.
A humanoid known as Rocknail Ripper.
Ripsaw is a demon bearing the title of overseer.

Morgroron is a pit lord stationed at Legion Hold, where the Legion equipped him with an anti-demon glaive prototype. Ordinn Thunderfist and Grokom Deatheye each describe the weapon as material for forging arms to use against the Legion. His combat routine includes Mortal Cleave, Rain of Fire and War Stomp.

Makazradon is a pit lord at Legion Hold, equipped by the Legion with an anti-demon glaive prototype. The weapon is sought as material for arms to use against the Legion. In combat, Makazradon uses Cripple and Fel Cleave.
A Sunfury warlock at Legion Hold, one of the Sunfury forces based in the area.
A Sunfury summoner at Legion Hold, among the Sunfury forces in the area.

Azaloth is a pit lord kept banished because he proved too powerful for the warlocks' demon-hunter training at the Ruins of Karabor. The Aldor and Scryers each seek to use his release as a distraction against Illidan's forces. When confronted, he threatens those he calls Illidan's lapdogs and vows they will pay for imprisoning him.
An Illidari jailor serving Illidan, responsible for keeping prisoners in custody.
An Illidari Slayer stationed in Shadowmoon Valley, this elite combatant attacks when engaged and uses a battle spell.
A mature Netherwing drake, this creature is found around Shadowmoon Valley. After being fed, it thanks the mortal who helped it.
An Illidari satyr serving Illidan, found in Shadowmoon Valley. It fights with a combat spell.

Neltharaku is a dragon concerned for his mate and children, and seeks to free enslaved Netherwing drakes from Dragonmaw control. He asks mortals to disrupt the Dragonmaw and gather nethervine crystals, whose magic he can imbue with his own energy to help the drakes break free. He praises those who aid his flight.

Oronu the Elder is Akama’s lieutenant at the Ruins of Baa’ri and receives Akama’s written orders daily. Both Aldor and Scryer agents seek those orders to learn whether the Ashtongue have recovered the Medallion of Karabor, which could aid their fight against Illidan.
Maiev Shadowsong fiercely defends independence in pursuing Illidan. Maiev rejects being a pawn in Akama’s scheme, demands release and insists on personally delivering Illidan’s death.

Akama conceals plans against Illidan, tolerating a reputation as the Betrayer’s servant. He attributes their former alliance to visions of his people’s survival and now seeks freedom with Maiev and his Deathsworn. He explains his secrecy by Illidan’s hold over his soul. Years close to evil have made him distrust his own fitness to keep a powerful artifact, while he trusts A’dal to safeguard it.
Akama's Deathsworn follow his lead in the struggle against Illidan; he speaks of leading them to Illidan's doorstep when the time comes.
A corrupted totem whose elemental nature is fire.
A corrupted totem whose elemental nature is earth.
A corrupted air totem, a summoned elemental focus rather than a speaking person. It is associated with the Fel Pits in Shadowmoon Valley.

Eykenen is an Ashtongue Corruptor, a Broken once counted among the powerful shaman who now defile the elements they revered. The title identifies Eykenen as a corruptor of earth; the name appears among those holding fragments of Akama's medallion, in the Fel Pits near the Hand of Gul'dan.

Uylaru is an Ashtongue Corruptor, a Broken once counted among the powerful shaman who now defile the elements they revered. Uylaru bears the title Corruptor of Fire and is named among those holding fragments of Akama's medallion; the quest account places Uylaru near the Fel Pits by the Hand of Gul'dan.

Haalum is an Ashtongue Corruptor, one of the Broken who were once powerful shaman and now defile the elements they revered. Haalum bears the title Corruptor of Air and is named among those holding fragments of Akama's medallion; the account locates Haalum at Netherwing Pass.
Dragonmaw Wranglers serve the Dragonmaw presence in Shadowmoon Valley. They can ensnare opponents with a net and may become enraged in combat.
Dragonmaw Subjugators are Dragonmaw combatants in Shadowmoon Valley. They move into combat and attack aggroing foes with Shadow Bolt.
A Dragonmaw drake-rider is found in Shadowmoon Valley.
A Dragonmaw shaman in Shadowmoon Valley can cast Lightning Shield in combat.
An enslaved Netherwing whelp is found in Shadowmoon Valley.
An enslaved Netherwing drake is held at Dragonmaw Fortress. The Force of Neltharaku can free it to fight its captor and fly away.

Kagrosh belonged to a three-person scouting party watching the Deathforge. Scout Zagran says he descended inside hoping to be a hero and fears he was killed. Kagrosh’s corpse lies discarded beside a walkway, where his pack can be searched for information.

Flanis Swiftwing was a skilled scout sent by Wing Commander Nuainn with two others to watch the Deathforge. He volunteered to infiltrate it; Stormer Ewan Wildwing fears the worst after his disappearance. Flanis’s corpse lies exposed there, apparently discovered during the mission, and his pack can be reclaimed.
A Wildhammer Defender appears across Shadowmoon Valley, serving as a guard among the Wildhammer forces.
A Sunfury Eradicator fights among Sunfury forces in Netherstorm, casting spells when engaged and again when badly wounded.
A Sunfury Blood Lord appears with Sunfury forces in Netherstorm as a named combatant.
Roldemar is an innkeeper in Shadowmoon Valley who offers shelter in the shattered lands, hearth registration and goods.
Caretaker Aluuro is an innkeeper in Shadowmoon Valley. Visitors can make the inn their home and browse goods, while the greeting speaks of shelter in the shattered lands.
A Shadowmoon Scout appears across Shadowmoon Valley, serving as a scout among the Shadowmoon forces.
A Felsworn of the Shadow Council, part of the council's forces in Shadowmoon Valley.
A Shadow Council Zealot, distinguished among the council's forces in Shadowmoon Valley by its zealous role.
Alieshor is a named flight master who directs travelers seeking air routes. When attacked, Alieshor summons an enraged gryphon and wyvern.

Overlord Or'barokh is a Horde commander in Shadowmoon Valley, concerned with keeping supply caravans safe from the region's dangerous wildlife while Horde forces are stretched by the Burning Legion. He directs grunts to clear those threats and treats the Legion's defeat as a chance to turn attention to other foes. His dialogue can be curt toward a shaman.

Researcher Tiorus studies Shadowmoon Valley’s lava-dwelling diemetradons, seeking to understand their resistance to heat. He pursues further observation with mechanical scorpions and becomes urgently focused on Felspine after learning of its size and Gnomus’s interest in it. Tiorus is an eager, driven researcher whose work turns into an enthusiastic search for protection from lava.

Warcaller Sardon Truslice serves at Shadowmoon Village and handles the reward for the order to kill Uvuros, issued by Overlord Or’barokh. His brief exchange on collecting the reward is warmly celebratory, with a playful troll manner of speaking.

Chief Apothecary Hildagard works in Shadowmoon Village, investigating its haunting. She warns that seeing the valley’s ghosts can change a person, crafts Spectrecles to reveal them, and asks for help clearing spirits from the village. Gorefiend’s story startles her; she recounts how Gul'dan placed the slain warlock’s soul in a knight of Stormwind, creating the first death knight of the Horde.

Thane Yoregar is a blunt, hands-on Wildhammer leader at the stronghold, focused on keeping its supply routes open while the Legion presses nearby. He puts soldiers to practical work, from clearing wildlife for caravans to assessing enemy plans, and relies on gryphon riders for reports. His rough humor and impatience mark a busy officer who expects people to act.

Zorus the Judicator studies Shadowmoon’s spirits and history among the Wildhammer dwarves, on ground he recognizes as ancestral to the Shadowmoon orcs. He treats the orcs as displaced even while asking that their ghosts be destroyed, and investigates disturbances through ash, crafted Spectrecles and reports. His dry humor gives way to unease when the spirits connect Teron Gorefiend to a history he thought settled.

Warcaller Beersnout is a Wildhammer Stronghold contact charged with Thane Yoregar’s order concerning Uvuros: adventurers are asked to kill the beast and bring back its fiery mane. His brief, colloquial replies promise a reward for success and dismiss anyone who has not done something special.

Gnomus is an inventor turned gourmet who recruits help to gather felfire diemetradon organs for his meals. He says his former partnership with Tiorus ended after he embraced gourmet living, and that Tiorus continued their research with Gnomus's inventions; he now wants Felspine before Tiorus can claim it. His eager replies and daily specials keep returning to food.

At Invasion Point: Cataclysm, Doctor Gutrick is a Shadow Council Overseer guarding the fel-reaver maintenance manual in a strongbox at the bottom of a ramp. The plan to recover the manual depends on taking its key from him, and the assignment warns that he is unlikely to give it up without a fight.

At Invasion Point: Cataclysm, Doctor Maleficus is a Shadow Council Overseer guarding the fel-reaver maintenance manual in a strongbox near the bottom of a ramp. The plan to recover the manual depends on taking its key from him, and the assignment warns that he is unlikely to give it up without a fight.
An undead rider associated with Karabor.
A Shadowmoon spirit who regards mortals as invaders of its home. It claims its fate is tied to Gorefiend, insists the spirits will not dissipate and threatens vengeance from Teron Gorefiend.

Nakansi rigs consoles to turn the Legion’s fel reavers against its supplies. The improvised remote controls work only briefly, and Nakansi warns that a stunt may attract Legion attention. Personal safety matters, but the mission and protection of Shadowmoon Village take priority. Nakansi coordinates the effort with Gulmok and Or’barokh.

Plexi works with the Wildhammer defenders on a rig to turn the Legion's Fel Reaver Sentinels against their own supplies and infernals. Informal and eager to get to work, Plexi values a useful technical manual even while mocking the Legion's literature. Plexi warns that remote control is difficult and can last only a short time.
Shadowmoon Harbingers are orc spirits haunting Wildhammer Stronghold. They regard the living as invaders and threaten vengeance, while their fate remains tied to Teron Gorefiend.

An ancient spirit bound to the Altar of Shadows, it initially draws others into restoring Teron Gorefiend’s armor and divining his whereabouts. Once the pieces are assembled, the spirit reveals that it is Gorefiend, imprisoned at the altar, and threatens to possess its helper and force the destruction of its captors. It later proclaims that Gorefiend has returned.

Vhel’kur is a dragon, spawn of Deathwing, who once called Netherwing Ledge home. After Gorefiend defeated him, the dragon remained there, flying an endless circuit and seething over that defeat. The Gorefiend armor quest identifies him as the one to defeat to recover the armor.
Elekk Demolishers are beasts found in the Ruins of Baa’ri area. They can use a special ability when wounded.

An Ashtongue Handler and servant of Illidan, found with other handlers at the Ruins of Baa’ri. The Ashtongue tribe is described as a fierce, ruthless group handpicked by Akama and deployed there in Illidan’s army.
An invisible Legion teleporter.
A Cleric of Karabor, one of a sizeable group stationed in the region.

Vindicator Aluumen serves the Aldor in Shadowmoon Valley, directing efforts against the Ashtongue at Baa'ri and Illidan's fel orcs at Ata'mal Terrace, a draenei holy site. He explains the Ashtongue's role in Akama's strategy and the fel orcs' occupation of the sacred ground.

Sanoru is a Broken and Akama's second-in-command at the Warden's Cage. He helps guard Akama's hidden resistance under a false appearance of loyalty to Illidan, and tests whether newcomers oppose Illidan before directing proven allies toward Akama's concealed hideout. He knows the Deathsworn understand Akama's true intentions.

Zandras is a satyr serving Illidan, watching the Warden's Cage from above its prison walls in Shadowmoon Valley. His watch puts him on the side of Illidan against Akama's secret plans. He uses Fel Shackles against nearby foes.

At the Altar of Sha'tar, Exarch Onaala directs the Aldor's response to Illidan's forces, investigating demon-hunter training at Karabor and urging action against its leaders. She recalls working hard to become an anchorite when female exarchs were rare; in her view, courage and conviction matter more than gender.
Scorchshell Pincers are hostile creatures in Shadowmoon Valley. They use Burning Poison in combat, making their venom their defining threat.
The Voice of Gorefiend is a speaking presence that offers its power and urges a listener to kill Karsius before being subdued.
Felboars are among Shadowmoon Valley's dangerous wildlife, alongside Vilewing Chimaera and Scorchshell Pincer. They charge in combat.
Vilewing Chimaeras are part of Shadowmoon Valley's dangerous wildlife, grouped with felboars and scorpions as a threat to Horde supply caravans. They attack with venom spit.
Felspine the Greater is the massive creature Researcher Tiorus seeks near the lava flow by Baa'ri for its hide. In combat it casts Fel Flames and Flaming Wounds.
Netherskate is a creature found in Shadowmoon Valley. Its combat behavior changes with its health, using separate abilities at mid-health and when badly wounded.
A demon known as a Spellbound Terrorguard, found in Shadowmoon Valley. It fights with spells, using a further spell when wounded.
An Arcano-Scorp in Shadowmoon Valley.
Lothros serves Illidan as a lieutenant at Illidari Point in Shadowmoon Valley. Altruis considers Illidan corrupted and Lothros part of the Illidari threat he is sworn to destroy.

Earthmender Sophurus belongs to the Earthen Ring and serves as a questgiver in Shadowmoon Valley. Sophurus offers a route into efforts to help the valley's tortured spirits: the associated quest sends the traveler to Earthmender Torlok at the Altar of Damnation. Sophurus is a local point of contact, while Torlok is the person the quest directs the traveler to meet.

Earthmender Splinthoof belongs to the Earthen Ring and serves as a questgiver in Shadowmoon Valley. The associated quest frames the valley's spirits as tortured and in need of help, then points the traveler southeast of Shadowmoon Village to meet Earthmender Torlok at the Altar of Damnation. Splinthoof is a local point of contact, while Torlok is the person named for the next conversation.
An elite mechanical sentinel.

Varen the Reclaimer is a Scryer quest-giver who directs efforts against the Ashtongue at Baa’ri and the Shadowmoon orcs at Ata’mal Terrace. He praises victories as service to the Scryers, calls a major success heroic, and greets returning agents courteously before offering another challenge.

Larissa Sunstrike is a Scryer investigator confronting Illidan’s demon-hunter training at Karabor. Cautious at first, she asks for weapons to confirm her scouts’ report; once convinced, she seeks to disrupt the training and directs a campaign against Varedis and his allies. Her replies remain measured: she hopes a distraction buys time and regrets that a valuable book must be destroyed.

Arcanist Thelis urgently seeks the Baa’ri tablets and Medallion of Karabor to aid the fight against Illidan. Thelis uses Akama’s written orders to trace the medallion’s fragments among the Ashtongue Corruptors and sees an opportunity to turn a Dragonmaw attack against its perpetrators.
A demon serving as a Cataclysm overseer.
Val’zareq the Conqueror belongs to the Crimson Sigil.
A vindicator associated with the Altar of Sha’tar.

A Kor’kron wind rider who urges allies to speak quickly because time is short. The rider coordinates collection of Illidari tabards for an espionage plan and asks for a flare signal when the disguises are ready, as the wind riders prepare the next assault from Shadowmoon Village.

Shadowlord Deathwail is Illidan's servant, defending the Heart of Fury at Ata'mal Terrace alongside his warlocks. He vows the crystal's power to Illidan and, when defeated, laments that he has failed his master.
Corok the Mighty is a giant at a meeting with Chancellor Bloodleaf on the Path of Conquest. Bloodleaf seeks the giants' strength for Illidan's cause; Corok asks what will happen if they refuse.

Chancellor Bloodleaf is Illidan's emissary at a meeting with giant Corok on the Path of Conquest. He urges Corok to lend the giants' strength, promising Illidan will reward those who help subdue the world's dissidents, then warns that Illidan's enemies are destroyed.
An Eclipsion Soldier is a rank-and-file Eclipsion combatant encountered while the Kor'kron clear a route and draw enemy arrows away from their scouting wind riders.
An Eclipsion Spellbinder is a combat caster serving alongside Eclipsion soldiers and cavaliers against the Kor'kron advance. It attacks with Arcane Missiles.
The Kor'kron wind riders seek to clear a path by thinning forces that include Eclipsion Cavaliers. This cavalier uses Battle Shout in combat.

Parshah is an arakkoa who grieves that Gul'dan's magic twisted the spirits of his people, whom he calls his brothers. He seeks to oppose the Dark Conclave by assembling a staff from objects of power, including a Sketh'lon war totem, the Rod of Lianthe, and feathers.
Asghar is named as the bearer of a Sketh'lon war totem that Parshah seeks. In combat, Asghar uses Shroud of Death.
Bahat is a humanoid in Shadowmoon Valley.
Smith Gorlunk is a named smith in Outland.

Gryphonrider Kieran is investigating the Dark Conclave arakkoa's preparations and the deserter mentioned in their records. After reading recovered journal pages, Kieran can make out fragments about a spell gone awry, casualties and a worsening situation, along with a note about the deserter. Kieran treats that lead as a way to learn what the arakkoa are planning.

Sergeant Kargrul is concerned that the Dark Conclave arakkoa are draining the life of orc woodcutters at the Sketh'lon ruins to fuel their magic. He seeks evidence of their plans and an explanation for their lingering spirits. Journal pages suggest an elaborate ritual continued until the arakkoa died; Kargrul also sees the deserter mentioned in the journal as a possible source of answers.

Behemothon, called King of the Colossi, speaks in defense of his children and the giants' independence. Addressing Illidan, he accuses him of attacking the children and breaking their pact, then declares that giants will never side with elves. His words express anger at the broken agreement and a firm refusal to ally with them.

A Wildhammer gryphon rider supporting the assault on the Illidari. The riders return to Wildhammer Stronghold to prepare for the next phase and can be called with a Wildhammer flare gun for espionage work; this rider asks whether you have gathered new information.
A Shadowmoon Soulstealer, a humanoid in Shadowmoon Valley.
A Shadowsworn drakonid serving Illidan in Shadowmoon Valley. It fights with cleave, Mortal Strike, and Sunder Armor.
Marcus Auralion is the Sha'tar's High General. Val'zareq's journal reports that the Crimson Sigil holds him in a crystalline prison at Crimson Watch on the Path of Conquest.
An elite Aldor gryphon guard is stationed in Shadowmoon Valley.
An Aldor Air Force alarm bot appears among the force's defenses in Shadowmoon Valley.
An Aldor gryphon guard post serves as an air-force defensive position in Shadowmoon Valley.
An Aldor Air Force trip wire guards a rooftop in Shadowmoon Valley.
A servant of Illidan, Shadowmoon Darkweavers are among the enemies the Aldor targets in its campaign to reclaim Ata'mal Terrace, a draenei holy site. In combat, this one casts Shadow Bolt.

A fel orc of the Shadowmoon force serving Illidan at Ata'mal Terrace, the Slayer is among the occupiers of draenei holy ground targeted by both Aldor and Scryer campaigns. When badly wounded, it can go into a frenzy.

Lord Illidan Stormrage demands obedience and responds to perceived incompetence with insults and threats. He dismisses a supposed hero as an insect and threatens a fate worse than death if his orders are not carried out.
The Shadowmoon Chosen is one of Illidan's servants among the Shadowmoon Clan fel orcs at Ata'mal Terrace. In combat it uses Uppercut and Whirlwind.
An elite Illidari Watcher bearing the title “The Crimson Sigil,” it appears with a small group in Shadowmoon Valley.
Remnant of Hate is an Aspect of Gul'dan in Shadowmoon Valley.

Karynaku is a netherwing dragon and the mate of Neltharaku. Held in chains by Zuluhed, she describes him pressing into her thoughts and asks for help freeing her and her children; she is willing to use his expectation of her submission against him.

Mordenai is a Netherwing ally in Shadowmoon Valley who is deeply concerned for the drakes and their flight. He urges help for exhausted drakes and speaks of the Netherwing’s stolen children, lost lands, and hope of rebuilding their home. He values compassion and proven loyalty, and supports a plan to infiltrate the Dragonmaw who occupy Netherwing territory.
A Shadowmoon Valley Eye of Kilrogg.
An ancient evil the Dark Conclave seeks to summon through a ritual empowered by Gul’dan’s magic. Parshah fears the death and destruction its manifestation would bring.
A Dark Conclave ritualist is a member of the group performing a summoning ritual at the lava pits. This ritualist channels the Dark Conclave’s magic.
Summoning Voidstorm in Shadowmoon Valley.

Battlemage Vyara refuses to accept defeat against Kael’thas and Illidan. She believes the Scryers’ survival depends on winning more recruits than Kael’thas, but expects a deadly contest once recruits run out. She values even small contributions of Sunfury signets and presses allies to keep proving their commitment.

Harbinger Saronen believes Illidan’s hold on the land is weakening and urges continued pursuit of the Burning Legion wherever it appears. Saronen accepts the insignias of Legion leaders and Shadow Council followers as proof of service to the Aldor, praising contributors as courageous allies of the priesthood.
A Dragonmaw peon who eagerly welcomes food and exclaims about hunger and mutton.
The Dragonmaw Ascendant is a Dragonmaw combatant that uses Cleave, Mortal Strike, and Uppercut in battle.
The Shadowwing Owl is a wild owl found in Shadowmoon Valley.
The Dragonmaw Skybreaker is a Dragonmaw combatant that opens a fight with a spell and casts again while engaged.
A Dragonmaw Elite is a Dragonmaw humanoid that holds its ground while out of combat.
A caster associated with the Altar of Shadows in Shadowmoon Valley.

Ja'y Nosliw is the Skybreaker General associated with the Dragonmaw Base Camp. He oversees a run of competitive flying challenges and greets riders' victories with surprise, praise, and warnings about their next opponent. His sharp banter values skill and treats the title of top orc as something to defend.
A named Remnant of Malice, titled an Aspect of Gul'dan.
A named Remnant of Greed, titled an Aspect of Gul'dan.
A named Remnant of Corruption, titled an Aspect of Gul'dan.
A named Remnant of Pride, titled an Aspect of Gul'dan.
A demon in Illidan's service, the Shadowhoof Summoner combines a summoner's role with spellcasting in combat.
A Lightsworn Vindicator who fights Illidan's forces, it taunts demons, calls them Illidan's lapdogs, and threatens to deliver a message to their master.
Anchorite Caalen challenges demons and Illidan's followers, saying he has a message for their master.
The Seasoned Magister is a seasoned combatant against Illidan's forces, taunting demons and saying it has a message for their master.
Fyra Dawnstar rallies the Scryers in battle, urging them to show Illidan's lackeys their steel.

Overlord Mor'ghor commands the Dragonmaw at their Shadowmoon Valley base camp and serves Illidan, praising his defeat of the demons. He expects recruits to work before earning a place in the army; he greets a death knight with contempt and threatens to leave him in the pit. He directs Dragonmaw attacks against Burning Legion forces in Nagrand.

Taskmaster Varkule Dragonbreath assigns manual work orders at the Dragonmaw camp, sending workers to collect Netherwing crystals, pollen, or ore for the camp’s needs. He mocks an inept worker, but greets an orc miner with a salute and pride: mining was how he got his start, and he calls the miner an orc after his own heart.

Yarzill the Merc is an inside ally of the Netherwing, helping undermine the Dragonmaw through covert sabotage. He promises the Netherwing will back these efforts and repeatedly urges the player to keep a low profile around Mor'ghor. He gives instructions in a whisper and intervenes to protect someone Mor'ghor threatens.
A goblin mercenary in Shadowmoon Valley.
Horus is an innkeeper. In a greeting, he warns visitors they cannot make this place their home and asks whether they want food, speaking in informally and haltingly.
Gug is an armorsmith who bluntly asks what a visitor wants, says they smell funny for a fel orc, and offers armor repair or goods in informal, halting Common.
Rumpus supplies reagents and poisons. He says he keeps stock for blood elves so Lord Illidan will not learn the Dragonmaw are failing to cooperate; he swallows hard and says they do not want that.
A Dragonmaw Enforcer is an elite enforcer. One asks who a visitor is and what they want, and another agrees to move while pleading not to be hurt.

The Mistress of the Mines oversees Dragonmaw mining at Netherwing Mines and says an infestation has left cargo scattered and miners unable to reach it. She assigns daily cargo recovery, which can be returned to her or her sister, and says the mines' Dragonmaw stranglehold must be restored.
A Dragonmaw pitfighter in Shadowmoon Valley.
Toranaku is found in the Netherwing Mines and urgently says they must leave, without giving a reason or destination.

Ronag the Slave Driver works in the Netherwing Mines. He dismisses concern about the escaped dragon, saying his side has plans for it, and orders the crazed Murkblood killed. Their cannibalism leaves him baffled; he responds with contempt, calling them stupid.
A Nethermine flayer troubling the Dragonmaw in the Netherwing Mines. The foreman reports that a dragon’s awakening stirred up flayers and ravagers, prompting efforts to cull them.
A transporter serving the Dragonmaw.
An Overmine flayer threatening Dragonmaw crystal harvesting on Netherwing Ledge. Dragonmaw orders report that rock flayers spread after the drakes were captured or driven away.
A beast known as Arvoar the Rapacious.
Barash is the den mother of the rock flayers targeted by Dragonmaw orders to protect crystal harvesting on Netherwing Ledge. Those orders name her consort as Arvoar.
Lady Sinestra is a named dragonkin presence in Shadowmoon Valley.
Nethermine Bursters tunnel with a passive Tunnel Bore effect, then use Bore and Poison attacks when engaged. They are aggressive creatures among the Nethermine's many bursters.
Black Blood of Draenor is a substance found through the Nethermine. Its name identifies it as a material of the region.
A Murkblood miner working the Nethermine country of Shadowmoon Valley.
Mine Car is a piece of equipment in the Nethermine.

Chief Overseer Mudlump oversees peons at the Dragonmaw camp and wears the boastful title “Beater of Peons.” His Booterang lesson treats fear and obedience as tools of the job, and he speaks of peons with open contempt. He expects new overseers to make their own disciplinary weapon, using materials such as Tyrantus’s hide.

A Murkblood foreman in the Netherwing Mines, he belongs to a band cut off from the exit after a dragon broke loose. The isolated Murkblood turned to cannibalism and mayhem, and the Dragonmaw want them killed.
A Murkblood overseer in the Netherwing Mines, he answers an approach with a grunt.

A Dragonmaw peon who resists the overseer's discipline, he cries out when struck by the booterang, apologizes, and says he will work; he also hopes to have a booterang one day. The Dragonmaw use the weapon to enforce obedience.

A Murkblood miner in the Netherwing Mines, he belongs to a band cut off from the exit after a dragon broke loose. The isolated Murkblood turned to cannibalism and mayhem, and the Dragonmaw want them killed.
A Nethermine Ravager, this hostile mine creature is among the creatures stirred up by the dragon's awakening. The Dragonmaw regard ravagers as a problem in the mines and seek help killing them.

Murg “Oldie” Muckjaw is a veteran Dragonmaw rider who takes pride in still outclassing younger flyers. He boasts of having tricks left despite his gray hair, then gives a brief, grudging acknowledgment when a challenger beats him.

Trope the Filth-Belcher is a Dragonmaw rider who describes himself as a worn-out cursed being and says the Dragonmaw gave him a chance. He taunts challengers about their flying and promises to shake them from his tail; after a hard race, he admits surprise at their performance.

Corlok the Vet is a Dragonmaw racing challenger who meets a challenge with mocking disbelief and threatens to hurl skulls while circling a rider whose flying he disparages. After a close contest, he grudgingly praises the challenger’s fight.

Wing Commander Ichman spent three years a Frostwolf prisoner, then left after his release to begin a new life among the Dragonmaw. He and Mulverick vie for the top-orc position. Ichman remains bitter about his captivity and turns that history into a taunting, mock bombing raid against a challenger.

Wing Commander Mulverick says he left as soon as the Dark Portal reopened and became a top gun for the Dragonmaw. He mocks the Alliance soldiers he recalls from the war and competes with Ichman for the top-orc position. A hard-edged threat gives way to praise for a rider who impresses him, whom he points toward Skyshatter.

Captain Skyshatter presents himself as an overwhelming force, using threats of meteors and darkness to discourage challengers. He says he accepts a race to make an example of the challenger for anyone else who might try. When defeated, he acknowledges the new top orc.
A Dragonmaw tower controller whose cry is “Mulverick!”.

The Dragonmaw Foreman oversees trouble in the Netherwing Mines: Nethermine flayers and ravagers have become a thorn in the Dragonmaw’s side, and he urges help clearing them out. His cleanup request is framed as a daily round, with enough work expected for that day.

Illidari Lord Balthas sees his brother Reth'hedron's allegiance as misplaced and a threat to Illidan's forces. With resources strained by the Sha'tar's war at the Black Temple, he chooses banishment over attempting to kill the powerful eredar. He plans to use a soul cannon attuned to their shared blood to drive Reth'hedron through the Twilight Portal and weaken the Legion's war against Illidan.

Commander Hobb is a Scryer commander at the Sanctum of the Stars who sets a trap for the Dragonmaw. He asks the player to use a signal flare to draw them into an attack and gives Scryer medals to serve as proof of victory for Mor'ghor. In the fighting, Hobb rallies the defenders and calls for help.
A Sanctum Defender is an armed guard who protects the sanctum. When fighting begins, it answers with ranged fire, adding direct force to the site's defense.
A Dragonmaw Skybreaker fights for the Dragonmaw, shouting battle cries and threatening opponents as it uses aimed shots and volleys against them.
A Dragonmaw Skybreaker fights for the Dragonmaw, shouting battle cries and threatening opponents as it uses aimed shots in combat.

Commander Arcus commands the Aldor's defense at the Altar of Sha'tar and is set on stopping the Dragonmaw. He asks for a signal flare to draw their raiders into a trap, then urges his soldiers to show no quarter. The medals he provides from fallen Aldor soldiers are meant as proof for Mor'ghor, even as Arcus prepares to defeat the Dragonmaw.
An Altar Defender is an armed guard stationed at the altar. When fighting begins, it answers with ranged fire, strengthening the site's defense through direct combat.
Drake Dealer Hurlunk describes drakes as his business and says he is authorized to sell them to the highest-ranking officers.
Niobe Whizzlespark is a master engineering trainer.

Jonathan Garrett is a master engineering trainer. His greeting jokes about squeezing knowledge from gnomes, crediting them with clever tricks, ways to escape trouble, cookies, and flying-machine craft.

The Shadowmoon Valley Flame Warden’s festival greeting welcomes visitors to honor the flame, encourages honoring fires in Alliance settlements, and urges desecrating Horde fires. Its message speaks from the Alliance side of the festival.

The Shadowmoon Valley Flame Keeper’s festival greeting welcomes visitors to honor the flame, encourages honoring fires in Horde settlements, and urges desecrating Alliance fires. Its message speaks from the Horde side of the festival.

place_records.text: You are in Shadowmoon Valley, a contested land in Outland where both the Alliance and the Horde hold settlements. The Horde keeps Shadowmoon Village and the Alliance keeps Wildhammer Stronghold, while the Altar of Sha'tar and the Sanctum of the Stars belong to neither side. Spirits, felboars and serpents roam the open ground, naga and Illidari hold the ruins and cisterns, and Burning Legion infernals strike from Legion Hold.

You are in Legion Hold, a fortress of the Burning Legion in Shadowmoon Valley. The Legion stocks and prepares its infernals here, and Shadow Council warlocks, terrormasters and deathforged infernals patrol its halls.

You are in Shadowmoon Village, a Horde settlement in Shadowmoon Valley. Blood Guard Gulmok directs its defense against infernals sent from Legion Hold, and Chief Apothecary Hildagard is trying to clear the spirits haunting the village. Grokom Deatheye, a weaponsmith, is working to turn the Legion's anti-demon weapons against their makers. It has a flight master, an inn and a stable.

You are in Wildhammer Stronghold, an Alliance dwarf stronghold in Shadowmoon Valley. Wing Commander Nuainn leads its defense against the Burning Legion's infernal attacks, and his troops are ragged and exhausted. Ordinn Thunderfist, a hammersmith, works to turn captured Legion anti-demon weapons into arms against the Legion. It has a gryphon flight service, an inn and a stable.

You are in The Fel Pits, a place in Shadowmoon Valley where enraged fire and earth spirits and corrupt totems are found. Eykenen and Uylaru, Ashtongue corruptors of earth and fire, were last seen here near the Hand of Gul'dan.

You are in The Deathforge, a Shadow Council forge in Shadowmoon Valley where infernals are launched toward Legion Hold. Deathforge guardians and summoners guard it, and scouts from both sides watch it. Stormer Ewan Wildwing fears for his fellow scout Flanis Swiftwing, and Scout Zagran says a scout named Kagrosh went inside and has not been heard from since.

You are in Coilskar Cistern, a place of the Coilskar naga in Shadowmoon Valley. Coilskar myrmidons, cobras and sorceresses are its main dangers, with enraged water spirits and a muckwatcher among them.

You are in Coilskar Point, a place of the Coilskar naga in Shadowmoon Valley. Grom'tor, son of Oronok, questions the naga here with violence and mocking offers of freedom, seeking a fragment of the Cipher of Damnation. A Coilskar commander among them pleads to be set free. Coilskar sirens, defenders and cobras are the dangers.

You are in Illidari Point, a place of the Illidari in Shadowmoon Valley where shocktroopers, painlashers and shadowstalkers are the dangers. The restless spirit of Ar'tor, son of Oronok, is still bound here, and his body is held by demonic crystals. The succubi who perform rituals at the site are led by Painmistress Gabrissa.

You are in Ruins of Baa'ri, a draenei village buried under lava in Shadowmoon Valley. The Ashtongue, a tribe of the Broken, dig here under Illidan's orders, and Ashtongue warriors, shamans, handlers and workers are the dangers, along with elekk demolishers and greater felfire diemetradons.

You are in Altar of Sha'tar, a post of the Aldor in Shadowmoon Valley. Commander Arcus leads its defense against the Dragonmaw, and Exarch Onaala directs the Aldor's response to Illidan's forces. It has a flight master, an inn and vendors.
You are in Ruins of Karabor, a set of ruins in Shadowmoon Valley. Sunfury eradicators, warlocks, summoners and blood lords roam them, with demon hunter supplicants and initiates.

You are in Ata'mal Terrace, a draenei holy site in Shadowmoon Valley now held by Illidan's fel orcs. Shadowmoon slayers, chosen, darkweavers and soulstealers are the dangers, and the Aldor direct efforts against the fel orcs there.

You are in Netherwing Fields, an open land of gigantic blue crystals in Shadowmoon Valley. Neltharaku, a dragon, seeks to free the enslaved Netherwing drakes from Dragonmaw control, and Mordenai, an Alliance ally, urges help for the exhausted drakes. Enraged air spirits and Rocknail rippers are hostile here, and Rocknail flayers gather near the crystals.

You are in Netherwing Ledge, an island off the broken shelf of Shadowmoon Valley, to the southeast. Dragonmaw peons and Murkblood miners are found in the Netherwing Mines, and nethermine flayers and ravagers are dangerous here. Toranaku, found in the mines, urgently says they must leave, without giving a reason.

You are in Warden's Cage, a stronghold in Shadowmoon Valley where Akama secretly plots against Illidan. His second-in-command Sanoru guards the hidden resistance and tests newcomers before sending proven ones to Akama. Maiev Shadowsong is also here, demanding her release. Illidari jailers and dreadwardens are hostile here.
You are in Eclipse Point, a part of Shadowmoon Valley where Eclipsion centurions, dragonhawks and archmages are hostile. Eclipsion bloodwarders and Illidari slayers are also dangerous here.

You are in Shattered Plains, hardened earth in Shadowmoon Valley. Ravenous flayers are hostile here, and Coilskar cobras and sorceresses are hostile too. Earthmender Wilda of the Earthen Ring, taken prisoner by naga, still seeks escape.

You are in Oronok's Farm, a hermit's holding in Shadowmoon Valley where Oronok Torn-heart, an Alliance trader, poses as a farmer. He offers shelter by his fire, a vendor and repairs, and flayers from a nest to the northeast have been attacking his animals. Coilskar myrmidons, cobras and sorceresses are hostile here.

You are in The Altar of Damnation, an altar in Shadowmoon Valley. Earthen Ring earthmender Torlok asks spirits for wisdom and warns that they may lash out. Gul'dan is here with several Remnants, Aspects of Gul'dan, and he boasts of razing and reforming the land.

You are in The Path of Conquest, an area of Shadowmoon Valley where Eclipsion soldiers are the most common danger. Eclipsion spellbinders, cavaliers and blood knights are hostile here too, along with sons of Corok.
You are in Eclipsion Fields, an area of Shadowmoon Valley where crazed colossi are dangerous.
You are in Sketh'lon Base Camp, a camp in Shadowmoon Valley where Dark Conclave talonites, scorncrows and harbingers are hostile, along with skethyl owls and felfire diemetradons.
You are in Sketh'lon Wreckage, a wreck in Shadowmoon Valley where Dark Conclave shadowmancers, hawkeyes and ravenguards are hostile. Asghar is among the hostile ones here, along with skethyl owls.

You are in Sanctum of the Stars, a Scryer base in Shadowmoon Valley with a flight master and an inn. Commander Hobb commands Scryer forces against the Dragonmaw, and Varen the Reclaimer directs the Scryers' campaigns against the Ashtongue and Shadowmoon orcs. Larissa Sunstrike investigates Illidan's demon hunter training at Karabor.

You are in Dragonmaw Fortress, a Dragonmaw fortress in Shadowmoon Valley where Dragonmaw wranglers, subjugators and shamans hold enslaved netherwing drakes. Karynaku, a netherwing dragon and the mate of Neltharaku, is held in chains here by Zuluhed, an ancient orc.

You are in Invasion Point: Cataclysm, a camp in Shadowmoon Valley where Nakansi, for the Horde, and Plexi, for the Alliance, rig consoles to turn the Legion's fel reavers against its supplies. Wildhammer Guards are posted here, and Shadow Council felsworn and zealots, Cataclysm Overseers and Fel Reaver Sentinels are the dangers. The Legion may notice such stunts.

You are in The Altar of Shadows, in southeast Shadowmoon Valley, where an ancient spirit is bound to the altar. It draws passersby into recovering the armor, cloak and truncheon of Teron Gorefiend, then reveals itself as Gorefiend, imprisoned there. Enraged air spirits are the local danger, and the Voice of Gorefiend urges listeners to kill Karsius.

You are in Netherwing Pass, in Shadowmoon Valley, where felmists, gas clouds, are found. Greater felfire diemetradons and enraged air spirits are the dangers here, and corrupt air totems stand among them.

You are in Magma Fields, in Shadowmoon Valley, where a Wildhammer Defender and a Shadowmoon Scout each serve their own side across the valley. Felfire diemetradons and felboars are the main dangers, and Deathforge smiths, tinkerers and guardians are hostile here too.

You are in Crimson Watch, on the Path of Conquest in Shadowmoon Valley, where Illidan's forces are the threat. Marcus Auralion, High General of the Sha'tar, is held in a crystalline prison here, according to Val'zareq's journal. Lord Illidan Stormrage demands obedience and threatens a fate worse than death for failure, and Eclipsion cavaliers and Illidari watchers are the dangers.

You are in Dragonmaw Base Camp, in Shadowmoon Valley, where Dragonmaw enforcers, peons and pitfighters are the main dangers. Murkblood miners, goblin mercenaries and a creature called Gug are hostile here too.
